subject: Failed to create shared library: Comparison between two codes

messages.author: 50e3f32525c093d1
messages.subject: Failed to create shared library: Comparison between two codes
parts:
Hi all,

I have been trying to get the following code to work:

dat <- read.csv("3Hedp.csv")
# Trying to reconcile naming conflicts; Order of data = Number
re <- as.numeric(dat$no) # Change the label to a numeric vector
# Note that the numbers are assigned by "sorting" the labels in alphabetical order
Nre <- length(unique(dat$no))
# Unique removes duplicated vector, we want to know how many groups of 
# data are there
N <- nrow(dat) # Total No of data sets
obsy <- dat$S    # Response variable in MeV
obsx <-  dat$E   # Predictors
erry <- dat$Stat # Error in MeV
set <- dat$lab # Get the labels as a vector

sepab <- c(1,1,1,1,2,1,2)
# 1 - a, 2 - b

# Inputting the quoted systematic uncertainty:
syst = c(log(1.043),log(1.078),log(1.039),log(1.034),log(1.055),log(1.030),log(1.030))
# In accordance to 
# Gei99 - 4.3%
# Kra87 - 7.8%
# Moe80 - 3.9%
# Zhi77 - 3.4%
# Cos00 - 5.5%
# Ali01_a - 3.0%
# Ali01_b - 3.0%

################
# Nimble Function, sfact (using nuclear package)
###############

sfact <- nimbleRcall(function(ecm = double(0),e0 = double(0),
                                  gi = double(0), gf = double(0),
                                  ri = double(0), rf = double(0),
                                  ue = double(0)){}, 
                         Rfun = 'sfactorHe3dp',
                         returnType = double(0))

samplerCode <-  nimbleCode({
  for (i in 1:N) {
    obsy[i] ~ dnorm(y.norm[re[i]]*mut[i], sd = sqrt(erry[i]^2 + y.scat[re[i]]^2)) 
    mut[i] <- sfact(obsx[i],e0,ga,gb,ra,rb,ue[sepab[re[i]]])
  }
  
  ## PRIORS - Get it to work first, understand later
  # e0:       eigenenergy
  # ga,gb:    initial reduced width, final reduced width [ga,gb = gamma^2]
  
  # energy eigenvalue
  e0 ~ T(dnorm(0, sd=1),0,Inf)       # positive since we see sigma peak 
  
  # reduced widths
  ga ~ T(dnorm(0, sd = 1),0,Inf)      
  gb ~ T(dnorm(0, sd = 2),0,Inf)
  ra ~ T(dnorm(6, sd=0.0001),0,Inf)
  rb ~ T(dnorm(5, sd=0.0001),0,Inf)
  
  # screening potential:
  ue[1] ~ T(dnorm(0.0,sd=0.01),0,Inf)     # certainly less than 10 keV
  ue[2] ~ T(dnorm(0.0,sd=0.01),0,Inf)     # certainly less than 10 keV
  
  for (k in 1:Nre){
    # Systematic Uncertainty as a highly informative prior
    y.norm[k] ~ dlnorm(log(1.0),sd=syst[k])
    y.scat[k] ~  T(dnorm(mt, sd=5),0,Inf)
  }
  mt ~ T(dnorm(0, sd=5),0,Inf) # Hyperprior
})

samplerData <- list(obsy = obsy    # Response variable
)

samplerConst <- list(N = N, # Sample size
                     Nre = Nre, 
                     re = re, # This is used to "iterate"
                     erry = erry,
                     syst = syst,
                     obsx = obsx,
                     sepab = sepab
)

samplerInits <- list(y.norm = rep(1,Nre),
                     y.scat = rep(0.01,Nre),
                     #ya = sfact(obsx,0.5,4,0.1,1,1,c(0.1,0.1)),
                     mt = 0, e0 = 0.5, ga = 4, gb = 0.1, ra = 1, rb = 1,
                     ue = c(0.001,0.001)
)

n.chains = 3
n.iter = 2000
n.burnin = 200


###############################################################
# (Alternative) If invoking Nimble MCMC stepwise (but more customisable)
##############################################################
ourmodel <- nimbleModel(code = samplerCode, constants = samplerConst,
                        data = samplerData, inits = samplerInits, check = FALSE
)
compileNimble(ourmodel)

However, upon compiling the model, this error appeared:

Error: Failed to create the shared library. Run 'printErrors()' to see the compilation errors.

P_24_MCMC.cpp: In member function 'double MCMC::calculateWAIC(int, int)':
P_24_MCMC.cpp:653:5: warning: variable 'Interm_1601' set but not used [-Wunused-but-set-variable]
 int Interm_1601;
     ^
P_24_MCMC.cpp:655:5: warning: variable 'Interm_1602' set but not used [-Wunused-but-set-variable]
 int Interm_1602;
     ^
P_24_MCMC.cpp:658:5: warning: variable 'Interm_1604' set but not used [-Wunused-but-set-variable]
 int Interm_1604;
     ^
At global scope:
cc1plus.exe: warning: unrecognized command line option "-Wno-ignored-attributes"
cc1plus.exe: warning: unrecognized command line option "-Wno-misleading-indentation"
      2 [main] make 24964 fork: child -1 - forked process 20452 died unexpectedly, retry 0, exit code 0xC0000005, errno 11
make: C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-36~1.0/share/make/winshlib.mk:13: fork: Resource temporarily unavailable
 568332 [main] make 24964 fork: child -1 - forked process 26552 died unexpectedly, retry 0, exit code 0xC0000005, errno 11
make: C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-36~1.0/share/make/winshlib.mk:13: fork: Resource temporarily unavailable
1201213 [main] make 24964 fork: child -1 - forked process 24836 died unexpectedly, retry 0, exit code 0xC0000005, errno 11
make: C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-36~1.0/share/make/winshlib.mk:13: fork: Resource temporarily unavailable
1953657 [main] make 24964 fork: child -1 - forked process 25424 died unexpectedly, retry 0, exit code 0xC0000005, errno 11
make: fork: Resource temporarily unavailable


However, if I were to make a slight adjustment to the sampling portion, ie:

from:

    obsy[i] ~ dnorm(y.norm[re[i]]*mut[i], sd = sqrt(erry[i]^2 + y.scat[re[i]]^2)) 
    mut[i] <- sfact(obsx[i],e0,ga,gb,ra,rb,ue[sepab[re[i]]])



to:

    obsy[i] ~ dnorm(ya[i], sd = erry[i]) 
    # Propagating the errors in observations of y
    ya[i] ~ dnorm(y.norm[re[i]]*mut[i],sd = y.scat[re[i]])
    mut[i] <- sfact(obsx[i],e0,ga,gb,ra,rb,ue[sepab[re[i]]])

The error disappeared! Hence, I'm wondering, what could have caused such a difference? I was trying to reduce the number of stochastic nodes to speed up the sampling process as it seems to run pretty slow as compared to JAGS (without some sort of "parallel" computing for different chains?)

Note: If anyone wants to try the code, the csv file is attached. The required function from nimbleRcall can be obtained via:

require(devtools)
devtools::install_github("rafaelsdesouza/nuclear")
library(nuclear)


Thank you very much for your time!

Best Regards,
HK Tan (Hong Kiat Tan),
Undergraduate Student | Physics 
National University of Singapore

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Failed to create shared library: Comparison between two codes
parts:
It's hard to imagine how an error during C++ compilation apparently related to forking could arise from the small difference in the nimble model.

Do you have a way to turn off any parallelization used by your compiler?

Have you checked if the curious behavior has to do with order of compilation?  (Start a new R session and compile them in opposite order.)  Some steps are taken once per R session, upon first use of compileNimble, and it is possible that is where your C++ compiler has a problem.

Are you calling compileNimble from within any parallelized code?
